prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: shared Vietnamese/English technology blog cover, landscape 16:9.
Primary request: show what a Forward Deployed Engineer does: hands-on software integration alongside a customer's team inside their operational workplace.
Scene: an editorial illustrated cutaway of a customer's factory office overlooking a working conveyor through a wide interior window. Foreground, two software engineers collaborate at one desk: visiting engineer wearing a clearly visible simple badge "FDE", typing on an open laptop; customer's engineer beside them points at a large operational display. The display shows a simple large connected chain: one purple software module, one distinct small coral adapter coupling, a grey database cylinder, ending at a green checked workflow card. It is a conceptual integration schematic, not a screenshot. The physical conveyor visible behind the glass establishes real operations. Make the people and hands-on work the main subject, with readable silhouettes, not tiny figures.
Style: sophisticated editorial gouache illustration with tactile matte brushwork, clean purposeful geometry, believable anatomy, warm ivory background, muted sage factory, indigo clothing and coral adapter accent. Soft daylight, comfortable professional atmosphere, strong dark/light hierarchy. Wide medium view, not sprawling isometric city.
Text (verbatim): "FDE" on the visitor badge, "LIVE" beside the green checked workflow. No other text, no pseudo code.
Technical constraints: the product is integrated through a distinct adapter into customer systems; no copied core modules or suggestion of a product fork for every client. No sales handshake, military imagery, robots, brains, magic AI powers, corporate logos, watermarks or decorative neon. Factory example is illustrative, not an actual company. Keep all essential people, schematic and labels in central 80% with generous crop-safe edges. At 320x180 the two colleagues, laptop and connected production workflow must read immediately.
